approach.method_basis: The Parent generates fresh molecular graphs, fits an accepted-score Gaussian process with a unit-linear three-tanh output transformation, and buys maxima of correlated draws mapped back to raw score units. It uses the transformed law’s integrated expectation for the existing stalled top-forty eligibility rule. The count kernel, fixed training noise, task-local archive, graph admission, survivors and breeding are all part of this measured Parent.
approach.novelty: Jointly learn one positive signal variance with the existing nine warp coefficients and propagate it through the complete conditioning law. Compare prospective predictions with an independently fitted fixed-amplitude unit-warp model on exactly the same accepted archive and purchased molecules. This tests the covariance freedom omitted by the Parent; the other issued positions change consumers or introduce a different predictive law.

hypothesis: On every original chronological accepted archive, retain m=mean(y), r=max(population_SD(y),0.001), t=(y-m)/r and the original count-Tanimoto K. Keep g_theta(t)=t+sum_{j=1}^3 a_j tanh(b_j(t+c_j)), with d=1 exactly and the original nine a,b,c coordinates. Jointly minimize the same total raw-unit Jacobian NLL over (theta,ell), s=exp(ell): L=0.5*g^T*C_s^-1*g+0.5*logdet(C_s)+n/2*log(2*pi)-sum(log(g_prime))+n*log(r), C_s=s*K+(0.05^2+j)*I. Here s is signal VARIANCE, not standard deviation or raw normalization scale. For alpha=C_s^-1*g, the unchanged nine warp derivatives are J_g^T*alpha-sum_i(J_gprime_i/g_prime_i); the new exact derivative is dL/dell=0.5*tr[(C_s^-1-alpha*alpha^T)*(s*K)]. The signal derivative includes both quadratic and log-determinant terms, and neither Jacobian nor raw normalization has a direct ell derivative. Use cross_s=s*K_Xq, mean_latent=cross_s^T*alpha and Sigma_s=s*K_qq-cross_s^T*C_s^-1*cross_s; no added query observation noise. The original correlated joint normals pass through the factor of the stabilized Sigma_s, then the unchanged inverse g^-1 and m+r scaling. The unchanged 128-point inverse-law expectation is the active eligibility coordinate. Signal fitting can change training influence, latent location, variance and correlation, the inverse law and consequently eligibility and paid choices; it is not a post-hoc residual temperature. Retain the independently estimated fixed-s=1 unit-warp law as the primary same-state comparator and the original raw GP as a secondary diagnostic. The hypothesized useful change is complete lower prospective pinball on actual paid labels; improved training NLL or changed parameters alone is not that result.

finding_summary.headline: Signal fitting lowers paid loss, but stop failures leave the complete experiment inconclusive.
finding_summary.insights: The added covariance freedom produced measurable changes in laws and purchases, so this result rules out lack of signal exposure as the explanation for an unresolved endpoint result. About 84% of the aggregate paid-loss reduction came from one objective, and two task cells worsened; the gain does not establish uniform or population-level benefit. All fitted signal variances exceeded one without reaching their declared bounds. Native solver acceptance still includes many function-reduction stops, so these are results of the registered finite fitting procedure. The chemistry report found broader scaffold coverage in four task pools but no specified stereochemistry, more molecules in the extreme size tail, and recurring unusual heteroatom bonds. A proposal method with chemically typed edits, controlled ring changes and deliberate stereochemical alternatives could address those measured coverage gaps; its endpoint benefit is untested. Prediction quality, molecular breadth and local parent gains do not establish mediation of optimization progress. The fixed-amplitude Parent’s earlier predictive result and the limits of older recipes remain unchanged; this experiment does not decide whether the wider approach should continue.
finding_summary.results: All 435 active and 435 independent fixed-amplitude fits were accepted, and all 4,350 original paid prediction pairs were recorded. Learned signal variance changed every predictive law, 402 purchase sets and 1,362 strictly changed paid identities. Mean pinball loss was 0.017172 versus 0.020303 for the fixed-amplitude comparator, lower in every seed mean and 13 of 15 task cells. Inclusive 90% interval coverage rose from 70.3% to 84.8%. Two tasks nevertheless failed to exit after the stop message. Their complete prediction records remain evidence, while their successful endpoints and two seed macros remain unavailable. Only seed 0 forms a complete score pair: its macro 0.567449 gained 0.013923 over the code Parent and trailed the same-seed formal Anchor by 0.082252. The full endpoint objective and task safety are unresolved. Under the registered complete-execution condition, the experiment remains inconclusive; the recorded predictive inequality is favorable.

molecular.headline: Ring-rich neutral molecules broaden most scaffold pools but retain unspecified stereochemistry and unusual heteroatom bonds.
molecular.overall_character: All 15 issued task/seed trajectories are present for this Child and separately for code Parent n-2723e9d54276. Each contains ten initial and 290 accepted optimizer records: 150 initial plus 4,350 optimizer records per side. All 9,000 recorded structures parse with RDKit 2023.09.6. This covers recorded molecules, not rejected proposals or successful evaluation. The Child has 13 ok task summaries and two buggy tasks: seed 1 median_2 and seed 2 drd2_docking, both reporting candidate did not exit after stop after 300 oracle calls. Those two task summaries omit final_top1, and their seed summaries have null val_score. Their execution receipts separately say retryable with exit_code 2; neither status is rewritten here. Parent has 15 ok task summaries. The exact frozen request says child_complete=false, paired_complete=false, child_seeds=[0], matched_seeds=[0], parent_seeds=[0,1,2]. Available trajectory labels from failed cells are retained for chemistry only; no missing endpoint, seed macro or complete paired score is reconstructed. The Child combines heteroaromatics, aryl carbonyl systems, aliphatic nitrogen rings and fluorinated fused or bridged heterocycles. Rings occur in 4,269/4,350 optimizer records and aromatic atoms in 4,216/4,350. All optimizer graphs are connected, have no formally charged atom, and specify neither atom chirality nor bond stereochemistry. Potential unassigned chiral centres occur in 2,460 Child versus 2,066 Parent records. Neutral graph notation does not establish solution protonation or absence of ionizable groups. N-halogen connectivity falls to 405 from 960 Parent records, while O-halogen connectivity rises to 334 from 35 and O-O single bonds to 225 from 59. These overlapping connectivity flags require individual chemical review; they are not measured instability or synthetic failure. Counts above 40/50/60 heavy atoms are 396/110/45 versus Parent 240/94/27, and molecular weight exceeds 500 in 997 versus 827 records. At the other tail, 71 versus 81 records have at most five heavy atoms. Typed/generic scaffold counts increase in four pooled task sets and contract in one; this supports conditional changes in breadth, not uniform collapse or chemical improvement. Descriptor conventions are fixed across both sides: accepted optimizer occurrences, including repeated identities across seeds; nonempty RDKit Murcko scaffolds with stereochemistry omitted, and generic scaffolds with carbon atoms/single bonds; binary radius-2 2048-bit chiral Morgan Tanimoto over every within-task pair after excluding records below ten heavy atoms. Pooled task similarities include across-seed pairs and are dependent descriptions, not replications. They are distinct from the model count kernel. Reported atom/ring/connectivity counts are derived from the recorded graphs; the digest counters remain string-level observations. No synthesis route, solution state, binding pose, biological utility, mechanism activation or causal endpoint explanation is established. The same median size coexists with more nonempty scaffolds and lower fragment-excluded similarity; neither metric establishes synthetic feasibility. All three task summaries are ok, while the overall seed panel remains incomplete. liabilities: Dense polycyclic junctions, thiol substitution and small carbonyl-containing rings in high-score examples require individual synthetic and stereochemical assessment.
Twenty-nine optimizer records have at most five heavy atoms; the opposite tail includes a 52-heavy-atom graph. No objective value here measures practical synthesis or biological utility.
missing_features: Stereochemically defined ring junctions are absent despite 592 records with potential unassigned centres; the leading structure alone has five such centres.

A controlled set of synthetically characterized alternatives to the congested fused/bridged frameworks is not demonstrated. The records cannot establish a missing target pharmacophore or a universal preference for fluorination.
per_task.score_gradient_reading: The cited seed-2 evaluation-293 polycycle scores 0.5674660587796533. The 52-heavy-atom extended aryl dicarbonyl molecule at seed 1, evaluation 30 scores 5.187613297020103e-29, and the one-oxygen molecule at evaluation 83 scores 3.3466049979681925e-24. Both large expansion and tiny fragmentation occur at the low end; these values are positive, not literal zeros. The observed high-score architecture is compact but topologically intricate, so compact size alone does not establish chemical plausibility or a required functional group.

transferable_gaps.evidence: None of 4,350 accepted Child optimizer records specifies atom chirality or bond stereochemistry; 2,460 contain a potential unassigned RDKit chiral centre, versus 2,066 Parent records. Complex ring junctions and substituted saturated rings therefore do not demonstrate controlled stereochemical coverage.
transferable_gaps.gap: Specified stereochemical output remains absent despite frequent potential stereocentres.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator would need stereochemistry-aware graph edits that preserve existing assignments and deliberately expose valid alternatives while retaining canonical isomer identity. This evidence provides no preferred configuration or measured benefit for adding such edits.

transferable_gaps.evidence: N-halogen occurrence decreases from 960 Parent to 405 Child records, while O-halogen occurrence increases from 35 to 334 and O-O single-bond occurrence from 59 to 225. Both ordinary heteroaromatic/amide structures and unusual covalent heteroatom motifs occur among supplied high-score examples; these are graph flags rather than experimentally measured liabilities.
transferable_gaps.gap: Consistent functional-group coherence remains incomplete across locally varied molecular families.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Chemically typed edits should expose coherent functional-group alternatives and retain interpretable local bonding during substitution and recombination. Actual accepted coverage must be measured; these observations do not justify treating every flagged molecule as invalid or imposing a hidden objective-specific template.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Child versus Parent counts above 40, 50 and 60 heavy atoms are 396 versus 240, 110 versus 94 and 45 versus 27, respectively. The largest Child graph has 88 heavy atoms, while supplied high-score examples often occupy much smaller size ranges. Molecular weight exceeds 500 in 997 versus 827 records.
transferable_gaps.gap: Controlled graph growth is incomplete, with an expanded extreme-size tail.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: Expose controllable growth, contraction and ring-closure edit scales while monitoring both central size and extreme tails. A finite output panel cannot specify a universal size optimum, and size control alone is not an established cause of better search.

transferable_gaps.evidence: Seventy-one of 4,350 Child accepted optimizer records have at most five heavy atoms, compared with 81 Parent records. The original digest includes tiny halogen-only, hydrocarbon and oxygen species with zero, extremely small nonzero or baseline labels; these distinct label regimes must not be collapsed into one outcome.
transferable_gaps.gap: Destructive edits still reach tiny fragments without demonstrated preservation of useful molecular architecture.
transferable_gaps.generator_implication: A task-agnostic generator could distinguish deliberate compact-molecule exploration from removal of nearly all molecular structure, and track which edits retain coherent connected architecture. This does not establish that all small molecules should be excluded.

method_name: Mol GA: rank-selected de novo graph evolution
method_thesis: Anchor the root in Mol GA: maintain a population of oracle-evaluated molecular graphs, sample breeding parents across high-ranked quantiles, generate new offspring through graph crossover and atom/bond mutations, and update survivors greedily after each observation. These are the proposal and selection mechanisms described by [Tripp and Hernández-Lobato (2023)](https://arxiv.org/html/2310.09267v1). Start from the supplied initial observations and incorporate newly evaluated offspring immediately, following the evaluator's announced batching. Repeated graph edits and recombination create an evolving search space; no corpus ranking, stored molecule library, pretrained model, or fixed candidate enumeration is needed. The causal hypothesis is that direct selection on task-local scores concentrates successive structural changes around improving molecules quickly enough to raise the final best observed score. The published evidence concerns a larger-budget AUC-Top-10 setting, so its transfer to this benchmark's final Top-1 objective remains a hypothesis.
